newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta, N Saskatchewan face frost risk Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Alberta, N Saskatchewan face frost risk Thursday.

text.p: Alberta and northern Saskatchewan were forecast to see a moderate risk of frost Thursday morning, Environment Canada said.
A moderate risk of frost was also likely in Alberta and all but southeast Saskatchewan Friday and Saturday mornings, Environment Canada said in its 10-day frost outlook.
A moderate risk of frost was forecast for the entire north and central Prairie grainbelt Sunday and Monday mornings with a slight risk on the south grainbelt Monday morning.
A high risk of frost was forecast for the north grainbelt Oct 1 to Oct 4.
A moderate to high risk of frost was forecast for the central and southern Prairie grainbelt Oct 1 and 2 and a slight risk Oct 3 and 4.

Alberta's overall crop harvest was 50 percent complete by Sept 23, behind 75 percent complete at the same time last year. Alberta Agriculture said. Saskatchewan's harvest was 52 percent done on that date versus 60 percent for the five-year average, according to Saskatchwan Agriculture. Manitoba's harvest was about 75 percent done by the week ended September 23, Manitoba Agriculture said.
Rain delayed harvest progress on the west Prairie.
